recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless a future THO governance issue changes the CLIA NamingSystem itself.
issue_request: FHIR-20182 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request asking to create or report the URI for CLIA Lab identifiers. Its resolution approved adding urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.7 to the identifier list until a future terminology registry existed.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by git commit bac96ea2f397ced9d976623d314a8d493fff40f8, which added a CLIA Lab identifier NamingSystem entry to source/namingsystem/namingsystem-registry.xml with OID 2.16.840.1.113883.4.7 and URI urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.7.
additional_context: FHIR-35932 later migrated the core identifier registry table to HL7 Terminology and changed the current build-scoped identifier-registry page to point implementers at THO. FHIR-37889 and FHIR-40117 removed the duplicate core NamingSystem registry bundle because THO is authoritative for this content. FHIR-36926 and Terminology Authority minutes show that the CLIA THO page was created and approved; the current THO NamingSystem-CLIA JSON contains the requested identifiers.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is appropriate because re-adding CLIA to core would contradict the later registry migration, while the current core page correctly delegates to THO and THO already has the CLIA identifier.

related_jiras.note: Migrated the core identifier registry table to HL7 Terminology and explains why current core no longer lists individual identifier systems.
Removed duplicate NamingSystem bundles from core because THO is authoritative for that content.
Removed the remaining empty namingsystem-registry.xml file from core.
Confirmed the CLIA identifier had been added to THO and cited the CLIA NamingSystem page.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core request to create or report the URI for CLIA Lab identifiers by adding urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.7 to the identifier list.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final approved seed request and target identifier URI.

evidence_items.summary: Implemented FHIR-20182 by adding a CLIA Lab NamingSystem entry to source/namingsystem/namingsystem-registry.xml with the requested OID and urn:oid URI.
evidence_items.learned: The issue was applied before later registry migration and cleanup changed where identifier-system content is maintained.

evidence_items.summary: The current build-scoped identifier registry page says the registered URI list migrated to HL7 Terminology and instructs implementers to use THO identifier-system URIs.
evidence_items.learned: Core no longer needs or should contain an individual CLIA row if THO contains the NamingSystem.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue removed the core identifier registry table after cross-checking that identifier systems had migrated to THO.
evidence_items.learned: This later decision makes the current core delegation to THO intentional rather than a missed CLIA application.

evidence_items.summary: The current THO CLIA NamingSystem is active and lists OID 2.16.840.1.113883.4.7 plus URI urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.7 as preferred identifiers.
evidence_items.learned: The requested CLIA identifier is present in the authoritative external registry referenced by core.

evidence_items.summary: Terminology Authority minutes record approval of the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) page tied to FHIR-36926.
evidence_items.learned: Terminology governance evidence supports relying on THO for the CLIA identifier rather than restoring core source content.
